method: Rebuild from primary text. Corp. Code §§1502, 17702.09, 2204, 2205 and 17713.09 and Rev. & Tax. Code §19141 were fetched from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read. The construing case was located through CourtListener. The previous clause cited only §1502 and §17702.09, which state the filing duty and say nothing about the penalty, the cure window or suspension — the three things the clause asserted. Assertions describe the REBUILT body; the previous body's errors are under priorDefects.
queries: Cal. Corp. Code §1502, §17702.09, §2204, §2205, §17713.09 and Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §19141 full text (leginfo)
"Corporations Code section 2205" statement of information suspension powers

assertions.text: the initial statement of information is due within 90 days after the original articles are filed, for both corporations and limited liability companies
assertions.note: §1502(a) for corporations; §17702.09(a) for LLCs and for foreign LLCs registering to transact intrastate business, where the 90 days runs from registration.

assertions.text: corporations file annually thereafter and limited liability companies biennially thereafter
assertions.note: §1502(a): 'and annually thereafter during the applicable filing period'. §17702.09(a): 'and biennially thereafter during the applicable filing period'. The previous body stated only the initial filing, though the corpus already carried the recurrence in a field used by the near-duplicate clause cal_ca_soi.

assertions.text: the applicable filing period is the calendar month in which the original articles were filed together with the immediately preceding five calendar months
assertions.note: §1502(d); §17702.09(c). This is a six-month window, not a single date, and the previous body's single {{soiDeadline}} date presented it as one day.

assertions.text: the Secretary of State sends a reminder about three months before the close of the filing period, and not receiving it is no excuse
assertions.note: §1502(d): 'The failure of the corporation to receive the notice is not an excuse for failure to comply with this section.' §17702.09(c) is to the same effect for LLCs.

assertions.text: on failure to file, the Secretary of State first sends a notice of delinquency, and only if no statement is filed within 60 days does it certify the entity to the Franchise Tax Board
assertions.note: §2204(a) for corporations; §17713.09(a) for LLCs. The previous body presented suspension as the direct consequence of lateness and never mentioned this cure window, so a founder who had already missed the date could not tell that one existed or how long it ran.

assertions.text: the penalty assessed by the Franchise Tax Board on certification is $250
assertions.note: Rev. & Tax. Code §19141, verbatim: 'the Franchise Tax Board shall assess a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250).' The previous body said 'a penalty' with no figure. Note the amount lives in the Revenue and Taxation Code, not in either section the previous clause cited.

assertions.text: the Secretary of State may waive the penalty for reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify the failure to file
assertions.note: §2204(f); §17713.09(f). The entity has a right to request that relief and the delinquency notice must say so (§2204(a)).

assertions.text: suspension of a corporation's powers is not the ordinary consequence of one late filing: it requires that the corporation failed to file for the period, has not filed for the preceding 24 months, and was certified for penalty under §2204 for that same period, after which a further 60-day notice runs
assertions.note: §2205(a)-(c). The previous body's 'can lead to suspension of the entity's powers' is true only at the end of this sequence, and the sequence is long. Stating suspension as a near consequence of a late filing misdescribes the risk in the direction of alarm.

assertions.text: while suspended the corporation's powers, rights and privileges are suspended except for filing an application for exempt status or amending the articles as necessary to perfect that application or to set forth a new name, and a suspended corporation is disabled from participating in litigation
assertions.note: §2205(c) for the text; Palm Valley Homeowners Assn. v. Design MTC for the litigation disability, which the section itself never spells out. This is the consequence that actually reaches a founder and the previous body did not have it.

assertions.text: the statement may be filed notwithstanding suspension, and on filing the Secretary of State certifies the fact to the Franchise Tax Board and the corporation may be relieved from suspension unless the Franchise Tax Board holds it suspended for tax reasons
assertions.note: §2205(d). The previous clause's defect note said restoration is by the Franchise Tax Board 'not the Secretary of State'; the section shows both are involved — the corporation files with the Secretary of State, which certifies to the Franchise Tax Board, and a separate tax suspension survives.

priorDefects: omitted: the $250 figure (Rev. & Tax. Code §19141), the only part of the penalty a founder can act on.
omitted: the 60-day cure window after the notice of delinquency (§2204(a); §17713.09(a)).
omitted: the recurrence — annually for corporations, biennially for LLCs (§1502(a); §17702.09(a)).
overstated: suspension presented as a consequence of late filing, without §2205(a)'s three cumulative conditions and second 60-day notice.
omitted: the disability that makes suspension matter — a suspended corporation cannot litigate.
citation-gap: the clause asserted a penalty and a suspension while citing only §1502 and §17702.09, neither of which contains either. The authority for what it asserted was never cited.
gaps: The LLC suspension path was not fully traced. §17713.09 supplies the LLC delinquency and penalty route, but the LLC counterpart to §2205's suspension mechanism was not read, so the rebuilt body states the suspension sequence for corporations and does not assert one for LLCs. An LLC reader is told the penalty route and not a suspension route; that is narrower than the law may be, and it is deliberately narrow rather than guessed.
Whether a suspended LLC suffers the same litigation disability as a suspended corporation was not verified from primary text and is not asserted.
The clause remains a near-duplicate of cal_ca_soi, which was not touched by this rebuild. The two will now disagree until cal_ca_soi is rebuilt from the same sections.

judicialQuotations.case: Palm Valley Homeowners Assn. v. Design MTC (Cal. Ct. App. 2000) 85 Cal.App.4th 553
judicialQuotations.quote: A Corporation Suspended Under Corporations Code Section 2205 for Failure to File a Required Information Statement Is Disabled from Participating in Litigation, as Is a Corporation Suspended Under Revenue and Taxation Code Section 23301 for Nonpayment of Taxes

judicialQuotations.case: Palm Valley Homeowners Assn. v. Design MTC (Cal. Ct. App. 2000) 85 Cal.App.4th 553
judicialQuotations.quote: If a corporation fails to file a statement under Corporations Code section 1502, fails to file a statement for 24 months, and has been assessed a penalty under Corporations Code section 2204 during that 24-month period, then the corporation is subject to suspension under Corporations Code section 2205.

currencyCaveat: Palm Valley is from 2000 and two things it says are no longer the law. It states that §1502 requires a statement 'every two years'; §1502(a) as repealed and re-added by Stats. 2020, Ch. 357 requires corporations to file annually. It also quotes §2205(c)'s exception as 'except for the purpose of amending the articles of incorporation to set forth a new name'; §2205(c) as amended by Stats. 2011, Ch. 204 now also excepts filing an application for exempt status and amendments necessary to perfect it. The rebuilt clause follows the current statutory text and relies on the case only for the litigation disability, which turns on the phrase 'corporate powers, rights, and privileges' that is unchanged.
